weather_line: Clearing in the hollows · ducks at rest · forty-seven degrees resolved

stories.headline: The Duck Bandit Revealed: Trail Volunteer Mira Ashworth, Survey Marker 7, and the Line Christine Ran That She Couldn't Stop Thinking About
body: The Duck Bandit is Mira Ashworth, age sixty-one, trail maintenance volunteer for the Harlan's Creek corridor, keeper of survey markers three through nine, and the woman who was sitting on the tailgate of a rust-brown Land Cruiser at the Marker 7 crossing on the morning of the expedition, eating a boiled egg, and watching Christine take the line that no one had taken cleanly in two seasons.

Ashworth — who introduced herself to Steve at the trailhead that morning as 'just the woman with the egg' — left the orange duck within forty-eight hours of returning home, having driven the bearing from Marker 7 to the front drive by memory and parked one street over. She stamped the numeral herself with a survey kit she has carried since 1998. The note read 'Survey 7. You know.' She reports that she assumed Christine would know immediately. Christine did know immediately. She simply wanted to see what the duck would do.

The forty-seven-degree angle between the two ducks — confirmed this morning by Ashworth herself, who came to the door with a third duck, green, small, and placed by hand on the bonnet between the other two — was not calculated. 'It's just where they ended up,' Ashworth said. 'Sometimes a thing lands right.' She drank a cup of tea, admired the flint stone on the kitchen table, and left. Lucy had met her on the drive in mid-July and approved of her immediately, which Lucy's attorney confirmed was the full extent of her client's prior knowledge.

stories.headline: Subcommittee Learns the Bandit's Name; Adjourns in a State of Conflicted Satisfaction; Three Members Cry
body: The Ministry of Magic's Duck Subcommittee — which has held forty-two emergency sessions since the orange duck's appearance, expanded its jurisdiction to cover numerals, footwear, directional bearing, and the colour spectrum, and drafted a combined seven-hundred-and-twelve-word memo it sent to no one — received the full resolution report this morning and sat in silence for four minutes.

The chair then stated, for the record, that the subcommittee was 'satisfied, if somewhat at a loss.' A motion was passed to retire the forty-seven-degree angle from active investigation and reclassify it as a landmark. The numeral 7 has been granted honorary status. The bootprint jurisdiction remains on the books in the event of future boots. Three members wept. This is considered a successful outcome.

stories.headline: Three Ducks Now on the Bonnet; Green One in the Centre; Steve Considers the Geometry; the Jeep Has No Notes at This Time
body: The Jeep, contacted this afternoon on the subject of the third duck, declined to comment but was observed to be sitting very still in a way that suggested quiet satisfaction. The three ducks — original pale yellow facing north-northeast, orange facing southeast, green facing directly forward — form what Steve described as 'a triangle that makes sense if you've been to the ridge,' which is the most precise thing anyone has said about anything this week.

Christine has taken a photograph. The photograph has not been filed with the Ministry's map committee, which has been waiting for something like this for years, and will simply have to continue waiting.

stories.section: Weekend Dispatch · A New Arc Stirs
stories.headline: Something Is Moving in the Harlan's Creek Corridor: Ashworth Reports an Unmarked Trail Spur Above Marker 9; No One Has Run It; the Maps Are Silent
stories.byline: By our adventure desk, filing early
body: Before she left this morning, Mira Ashworth mentioned — briefly, offhandedly, while rinsing her cup — that above survey Marker 9, roughly four hundred yards northeast of the Keeps Ridge crossing, there is a spur that doesn't appear on any trail chart she has maintained or seen. She has walked its first hundred yards. It climbs. 'It's a line,' she said, in the tone of a woman who has been waiting for the right people to exist before mentioning it.
She did not say more. She put her cup on the drainer and left. Steve found the area on the edge chart this evening. The edge of the chart is where the paper ends. The spur would begin just past it.

The Prophet's expedition desk has opened a preliminary file. The file currently contains one note in Steve's handwriting, the word 'Saturday?' and a small question mark that looks like it means business.

familiars_corner: Lucy: has confirmed, via a statement released through her attorney, that she met Mira Ashworth on the drive on 19 July, assessed her boot tread, found it acceptable, and made a professional decision not to escalate. The attorney notes that this is called discretion and that Lucy has been practising it for years.

Ellie: spent the morning introducing herself to the green duck, which is the same green as the good blanket, and therefore almost certainly the same duck, just from a different angle. Ellie considers this a reasonable hypothesis and is sitting on it to see what hatches.

Jersey: was on Christine's lap when Ashworth came to the door, remained on Christine's lap through the full revelation, and has submitted a brief noting that he was present for the entire resolution and contributed warmth throughout, which he considers decisive.
founding_editor_note: The triangle makes sense if you know where you've been. Most good things are like that. — D.

in_brief.sport: Weekend Lifting Results: the flint stone on the kitchen table has not moved; Christine's form, by all accounts, remains impeccable.
in_brief.forecast: Saturday clearing · a new spur opens northeast · bring the edge chart and something to write with.

storyline_updates.title: The Duck Waits
storyline_updates.summary: Resolved Saturday morning. The Duck Bandit is Mira Ashworth, trail volunteer, keeper of survey markers 3–9, witness to the line Christine ran at Marker 7 crossing. She left the orange duck in tribute, stamped it with her own survey kit, and placed the note herself. The third duck — green, small — was placed by hand on the bonnet this morning between the original two, forming a triangle. The forty-seven-degree angle was not calculated; it simply landed right. Lucy approved of Ashworth in mid-July and exercised professional discretion. The arc is closed.

storyline_updates.title: Above Marker 9
storyline_updates.summary: Day 1: Mira Ashworth mentioned, before leaving, an unmarked spur above survey Marker 9 — four hundred yards northeast of the Keeps Ridge crossing, not on any chart, climbing into unmapped ground. She has walked its first hundred yards. She did not say more. Steve has found the edge of the chart where the spur would begin. A preliminary expedition file has been opened. Day 2 should deepen the mystery of the spur: perhaps a detail from Ashworth's second contact (a follow-up owl, or a rough sketch she left behind), or a first attempt to locate the spur's mouth on the ground — a Saturday drive up the corridor, a glimpse of the turnoff, something that suggests the line is real and worth running.
